# Witnessory

> An observatory of the internet's move to post-quantum cryptography: how far servers have moved (key exchange,
> certificates, SSH, DNSSEC, routing, mail) and how close quantum computers are to breaking what has not, measured
> from probes on several networks whose every reading is signed (Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65). Free to read.

## Data

- https://witnessory.org/view.json: the current view, refreshed hourly. `layers.<layer>.headline` holds the headline
  figures (each with `median`, `min`, `max` and `n` across probes); `params.as_of_utc` says when; `view_sha256` names
  the exact computation. Cross-origin requests are allowed.
- Layers measured monthly (keys: post-quantum TLS on the top 10,000 sites; ssh; dnssec) appear once each month's scan
  has run.

## Check one site

- `GET https://check.witnessory.org/api/check?domain=example.org`: whether a browser gets post-quantum key exchange
  from that site, signed. Description: https://check.witnessory.org/openapi.json and
  https://check.witnessory.org/llms.txt. Free, no key; 20 new checks an hour from one address.

## Run a probe

- https://witnessory.org/probe.html: install a probe (Linux, Raspberry Pi, Windows, Docker, Python) and measure from
  your own network. Source and terms: https://github.com/witnessory/probe (Apache 2.0).
- https://coordinator.witnessory.org/probes.json: every active probe's network and country, counts by country and
  network, and the probes with the most credits (also as a page at /probes). One probe: /p/<probe id>.json.

## Contact

- Security: security@witnessory.org (https://witnessory.org/.well-known/security.txt).
